findings.title: TLS certificate is self-signed
findings.description: The presented certificate is self-signed and not issued by a trusted CA.
findings.why_it_matters: Self-signed certificates do not protect against man-in-the-middle attacks unless clients are configured to pin them.
findings.recommendation: Obtain a certificate from a public CA (e.g. Let's Encrypt) or pin the certificate on all clients.

findings.title: TLS certificate hostname mismatch
findings.description: The certificate does not cover the hostname being scanned (SANs: none).
findings.why_it_matters: A certificate for the wrong hostname triggers browser warnings and can signal a misconfigured or intercepted connection.
findings.recommendation: Issue a certificate that includes the scanned hostname in its SANs.
